$$(px+2)(7x^{2}-qx+6)=35x^{3}-11x^{2}+20x+12$$

The equation is true for all values of $x$, where $p$ and $q$ are constants. What is the value of $pq$?
explanation: Choice B is correct. Expanding the left side: $(px+2)(7x^2-qx+6) = 7px^3 - pqx^2 + 6px + 14x^2 - 2qx + 12 = 7px^3 + (-pq+14)x^2 + (6p-2q)x + 12$. Matching the $x^3$ coefficients: $7p = 35$, so $p = 5$. Matching the $x^2$ coefficients: $-pq + 14 = -11$, so $pq = 25$.
